Name: David Tussey
Question: Can someone justify electric vehicles to me?
Answer: From my perspective, it’s a national security imperative. The US foreign policy in the Middle East has been driven for the last 50 years by our dependence on cheap foreign oil, often from nations that do not share our national interests. And oil companies (ExxonMobile, Chevron, Phillips, etc.) are driven by profit, not by national security interests. They sell to the highest bidder on the global market. Accordingly, if the US could free itself from dependency on foreign oil, we could enact more sensible, stronger policies in the Middle East and elsewhere. So I see this as a necessary element of a more rational foreign policy. There are many, many sources for electricity (solar, wind, nuclear, hydro, etc.). But there’s only one place to get gasoline - fossils. Oh and there’s the “save the planet from runaway global warming” aspect. That’s kind of important too.
